about: What an extension changes in igni, and where two extensions collide: cases igni (src/ember_code/extensions/impact.py) and igni server (app/services/identity/impact.py) both run, so the two implementations of one rule give the same answers. The copy in igni's tests/fixtures/ is the original; igni server's tests/fixtures/ holds the same file, and each repository's test fails when its sibling checkout's copy differs. A case's optional "reserved" is the claims igni keeps for itself (its own commands), passed to the resolver as such. A manifest's "permissions.intercepts" are never claims: interceptors chain in priority order. A case's "enforce" lists, per extension, what is switched off ("off") and the edits that land nowhere because another extension's override has no section they name ("dropped").

cases.name: two extensions editing different sections of one prompt do not collide
two extensions replacing one section collide, and undecided it is off for both
inserts and appends from several extensions never collide
two overrides of one prompt collide
an override does not collide with edits of the same prompt; what it has no section for is dropped
an exclusive override collides with everyone who edits that prompt
an exclusive override that wins switches every other extension's edits of that prompt off
edits that win over an exclusive override switch the override off
a decided collision switches off only the loser's claim
a decided collision and an undecided one side by side
a decision does not cover an extension it did not consider
a decision among more extensions holds between fewer of them
when the winner is not there, everyone who is lost
an agent is a prompt like any other: its overrides and its frontmatter collide
an override of an agent keeps its frontmatter: edits of it land, the rest drop while the override holds
filling one anchor is a claim too
a condition does not avoid a collision
each prompt is its own: an exclusive override of the main prompt does not touch plan mode
namespaced things never collide
one of igni's own commands is nobody's: off for every extension, nothing to decide
extensions intercepting one event never collide, whether they reject it or change it
